server.maintainedFrom: the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server

tools.label: ESLint
tools.why: nothing checks the frontend sources, so a wrong import is found by the build or not at all
tools.legacyWhy: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8

tools.label: Stylelint
tools.why: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly

tools.label: Psalm
tools.why: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does

tools.label: PHPUnit
tools.why: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change

tools.label: PHP-CS-Fixer
tools.why: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command

tools.label: REUSE
tools.why: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for

tools.label: EditorConfig
tools.why: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does

lines: Version drift: appinfo/info.xml says 5.5.17, package-lock.json packages[""] says 5.5.14.

make version of ncmake bumps info.xml, composer.json and package.json and re-syncs package-lock.json in one step, so they cannot drift apart. ncmake's lint-version workflow fails a push or a pull request on exactly this drift. The App Store and the server read info.xml, npm and composer read their own manifest. Whichever is behind, a release ends up carrying more than one version number, and only one of them reaches the user.
2 links of appinfo/info.xml lead nowhere:
<documentation><user> https://github.com/nextcloud/mail/blob/main/doc/user.md: HTTP 404
<documentation><admin> https://github.com/nextcloud/mail/blob/main/doc/admin.md: HTTP 404
The App Store page shows these links as they are; a reader who follows one ends on an error page.
3 PHP extensions are required by composer but not listed as <lib> in appinfo/info.xml:
filter (jeremykendall/php-domain-parser)
iconv (bytestream/horde-stringprep, sabberworm/php-css-parser)
intl (bytestream/horde-stringprep)

A Nextcloud server need not load them. The server checks <lib> before it enables the app; composer only checks where it runs. Without the <lib> the app is enabled anyway and the first call into a missing one fails at runtime.
resources/ is read at run time and is not in the shipped file set: lib/Dns/Resolver.php:23 reaches it through __DIR__.

A release ships only the paths of the keep set, so the tarball lacks it and the app fails in the code that reads it, while the build and the packing pass. In ncmake.mk, keep_extra += resources ships it.
The licence is stated differently: agpl (appinfo/info.xml), AGPL-3.0-only (package.json).
Whoever redistributes the app has to pick one of them, and the App Store shows the one from info.xml.
agpl in appinfo/info.xml is a deprecated App Store value, shown there as AGPLv3+, which is AGPL-3.0-or-later. An SPDX id there needs a <nextcloud> min-version of 31 or higher.
Declares Nextcloud 30 to 33; the oldest maintained major is 33 (the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server), the newest released 35 (the release tags of nextcloud/server).
min-version 30 reaches below the oldest maintained major (33), which means the code has to keep working with APIs that are no longer tested upstream.
appinfo/info.xml caps PHP at max-version 8.4.
A server on a newer PHP refuses to enable the app, so this cap has to be raised deliberately with every PHP release, not left where it was.
Node stated as ^22.0.0 (package.json engines.node), false (test.yml).
Not stated in .nvmrc, so nothing keeps the other places from drifting away from it.

Tooling in the checkout: ESLint (.eslintrc.js, superseded form), Stylelint (stylelint.config.js), Psalm (psalm.xml), PHPUnit (tests/phpunit.integration.xml), PHP-CS-Fixer (.php-cs-fixer.dist.php), REUSE (REUSE.toml), EditorConfig (.editorconfig).

ESLint is configured in .eslintrc.js: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8.
7 declared packages are named nowhere in the checkout: @ckeditor/ckeditor5-source-editing, @ckeditor/ckeditor5-table, @vue/babel-preset-app, vue-click-outside, vue-scroll, autoprefixer, url-loader.

Searched as literal names over 1,316 files, package.json excluded apart from its non-dependency fields, lockfiles excluded; then as an ESLint shorthand, as what TypeScript takes from a tsconfig, and as a peer of an installed package in package-lock.json. A package loaded some other way is not named anywhere either, so this is a list to check, not a list to remove.
appinfo/info.xml links its repository and its bug tracker.
PHP 8.1 is the floor in appinfo/info.xml and in composer.json, platform 8.1.
package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) and composer.lock in the checkout.
The ncmake bootstrap stub is in place (21 lines).
make reads GNUmakefile and never Makefile; it runs only with make -f <name>.
